headline: Nitrogen makes up 78% of every breath—yet your body can barely use it directly
universal_truth: Being surrounded by something doesn't mean we can access it
fun_facts: Nitrogen is 78% of air but so chemically stable that most organisms can't use it directly
Lightning can 'fix' nitrogen, making it available to plants—nature's fertilizer factory
All the protein in your body requires nitrogen, yet you can't get it from breathing
discussion_questions: What are you surrounded by that you can't directly access or use?
Why might nature make something essential so difficult to obtain?
How do barriers to access create interdependence?

hook.script: With every breath, you inhale mostly nitrogen—78% of air is nitrogen. You breathe it in. You breathe it out. Unchanged. Your body is swimming in nitrogen but can barely use it. The most abundant gas is also one of the most inaccessible.

cliff.script: Every protein in your body requires nitrogen. Your DNA needs nitrogen. Yet you can't absorb it from the air around you. If you're surrounded by nitrogen and need it for survival, how do you get it?
cliff.prompt: How do living things get nitrogen if not from air?

options.text: Bacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen into usable forms; plants absorb it; we eat plants
options.response: Yes. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria are the hidden heroes that make nitrogen accessible to all life.

options.text: Water contains dissolved nitrogen that plants and animals can absorb
options.response: Some nitrogen is in water, but the primary pathway is through bacteria...

fact1.title: The Triple Bond
fact1.script: Nitrogen atoms bond to each other with a triple bond—one of the strongest in nature. This makes nitrogen gas incredibly stable, almost inert. Breaking that bond to use nitrogen requires enormous energy or specialized biology.

fact2.title: Bacterial Heroes
fact2.script: Certain bacteria can do what we cannot—fix nitrogen. They break the triple bond and convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia, which plants can absorb. These bacteria live in soil and in root nodules of legumes. All protein traces back to their work.

fact3.title: Lightning Factories
fact3.script: Lightning also fixes nitrogen—the immense energy breaks nitrogen bonds, creating nitrogen oxides that rain into soil. A single thunderstorm can fertilize acres of land. Nature has multiple systems for cracking this essential but stubborn element.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Abundance doesn't guarantee access. Nitrogen teaches that being surrounded by something doesn't mean you can use it. Value the intermediaries—the bacteria, the processes, the connectors—that make the inaccessible available.

outro.script: That's Day 74. Tomorrow, we'll discover the simplest element—hydrogen. Until then, appreciate the invisible bacteria that make your proteins possible.

growTrack.title: Access vs. Abundance - Find Your Intermediaries
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify what makes the inaccessible accessible
growTrack.activity: What valuable thing are you surrounded by but can't access directly—information, opportunity, community? Who or what could be your 'nitrogen-fixing bacteria'—the intermediary that converts potential into usable form? Seek that connector.
